data.narrative:
Xona Space Systems is a Series C-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $281M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 7 private companies in the same sector and stage (ranging from Series B to Series D), with a median valuation of $2.0B across that cohort. Five public space and aerospace comps were identified (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) though revenue-based multiples could not be applied given the lack of public financial disclosure from the target.

Two methods were triangulated. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement to the $281M capital raised, implying a valuation of $478M. The peer-median approach references the 7 same-sector peers at comparable or adjacent stages, where the median valuation stands at $2.0B, with a range spanning $1.15B to $8.0B. This range reflects significant dispersion within the cohort—Sierra Space commands $8.0B at Series C while Cowboy Space Corporation trades at $2.0B in Series B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $406M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median cross-section of $1.2B. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data to anchor public-comp multiples and material stage/product-maturity differences across peer comparables. The wide peer range underscores the sensitivity of frontier-aerospace valuations to execution risk and customer traction.
